name: sandbox
description: Per-space cloud sandbox (Vercel Sandbox microVM) bound to a Decillion space: run shell commands, install packages, write and read files, expose ports
usecases: you need to actually run something instead of describing it — shell commands, installs, builds, tests, scripts
you need a file to exist on a real machine, or to read one back
you want to hand the team a running service: expose a port and share its public URL
you want work to persist for the whole project — the sandbox is shared by everyone in this space and survives between turns
howToTalk: Signal it with `function` naming the operation: `exec` (default) runs a shell line — pass `command`, optionally `cwd`, `env`, `timeout_ms` — and returns `stdout`, `stderr` and `exit_code`; `write` takes `path` + `content`; `read` takes `path`; `mkdir` takes `path`; `list_dir` takes `path`; `info` reports status and the public URLs of exposed ports; `start` boots the machine and `stop` puts it to sleep keeping its files. The space is already bound — never pass a space id.
prompt: Use this to actually DO work on a machine instead of only describing it: run shell commands, install dependencies, clone repos, execute build/test suites, write and read files, and expose a port so the humans in the space can open what you built. Every space has exactly one sandbox and it is shared by the whole team, so files you write persist between turns and other agents in the space see them. The sandbox is addressed by the space it belongs to — you never create or choose one. Name the operation with `function`: exec (default), write, read, mkdir, info, start, stop.

function.description: operation: exec (default) | write | read | mkdir | list_dir | info | start | stop

command.description: for exec: the shell command line, e.g. "npm install && npm test"

env.description: optional extra environment variables for this command

path.description: for write/read/mkdir/list_dir: the file or directory path

tools.name: exec
tools.desc: run a shell command in the space's sandbox and return stdout, stderr and the exit code; the whole line is run through `sh -c`, so pipes, redirects and && work

function.desc: the operation to run: exec | write | read | mkdir | info | start | stop (default exec)

command.desc: the shell command line to run, e.g. 'npm install && npm test'

cwd.desc: optional working directory (defaults to the sandbox home directory)

env.desc: optional extra environment variables for this command

path.desc: for write/read/mkdir: the file or directory path

tools.name: write
tools.desc: create or overwrite a file in the space's sandbox

path.desc: file path, absolute or relative to the home directory

cwd.desc: optional base directory for relative paths

tools.name: read
tools.desc: read a file back out of the space's sandbox

cwd.desc: optional base directory for relative paths

tools.name: mkdir
tools.desc: create a directory in the space's sandbox

tools.name: list_dir
tools.desc: list the entries of a directory as structured {name, type, size} rows (directories first); read-only, powers the file-explorer front-end

path.desc: directory to list (default the sandbox home directory)

tools.name: info
tools.desc: report the space's sandbox status, runtime, working directory and the public URLs of any exposed ports

resume.desc: resume the sandbox if it is stopped (default false)

tools.name: start
tools.desc: boot or resume the space's sandbox from its snapshot before a burst of work

ports.desc: optional ports to expose publicly when it has to be created

tools.name: stop
tools.desc: stop the space's sandbox VM, keeping its filesystem — the next command resumes it

tools.name: create
tools.desc: provision the sandbox bound to a space (called by the platform when a space is created; agents should use start instead)

space_id.desc: the Decillion space id the sandbox is bound to

tools.name: delete
tools.desc: destroy the sandbox bound to a space and all of its snapshots (called by the platform when a space is deleted)

space_id.desc: the Decillion space id whose sandbox is being destroyed
